answer: Picture a basalt quarry where identity is a tenancy, not a name. Each key must seal a minimum deposit in a public vault and pay rent every epoch that is burned, never refunded. Rent rises with the number of live keys, so idle sybils bleed capital each round while honest agents cover it with mining rewards. A rotating liveness challenge must also be answered, and the ledger keeps a mirror of every payment, so one funded wallet cannot be cloned or share its rent across many keys. Cost to an attacker: M vaults funded plus M rents burned forever — a recurring drain, not one cheap registration.
